label: Mean annual rainfall
notes: Less rain = worse. ~25 km source.

label: Inter-annual rainfall variability
Consecutive dry days (annual max)
notes: Dry day = pr < 1 mm.

label: Aridity index (P/PET; Hargreaves PET)
notes: Annual P / PET per model and period, PET by Hargreaves (FAO-56 eq. 52) from tasmax/tasmin, then ensemble median as for the other 201 metrics. Not standardised per cell, so the baseline has spatial contrast and future periods include warming-driven PET. Overlaps with annual_rainfall (P is the numerator): check correlation before weighting.

label: Subsistence cropland per household (5 km neighbourhood)
notes: Alternative to smallholder_presence (do not use both). SANLC class 41 ha within 5 km / Census 2011 households within 5 km (households spread on SANLC settlement). Already on the template grid, so resample = near. More cropland per household = more reliance on rainfed crops = worse. Cells without households are NA. trim 0.02 because of a long tail. Ward version: subsistence_cropland_per_household_wards2011_1km.tif.

label: Share of cell under subsistence/small-scale crops
notes: Average of the 20 m 0/1 layer = fraction of the 1 km cell.

label: Long-term grazing capacity
notes: Higher capacity = less vulnerable.

label: Mean annual grassland GPP 2022-2024
source: Global Pasture Watch pantropical calibrated grassland GPP v1.2, 30 m (112/208)
notes: Sensitivity alternative to grazing_capacity (do not use both). Lower GPP = less forage = worse. Mean of 2022-2024 on the 30 m grid (0 = no grassland, NA), averaged to 1 km over grassland pixels.

label: Livestock density (cattle + sheep + goats)
notes: TLU = 0.7 cattle + 0.1 sheep + 0.1 goats (FAO SSA weights), from GLW4 head/km2 (dasymetric, ~10 km). More animals per km2 = more livestock competing for the same springs, rivers and dams and more assets lost in drought. Source grid ~10 km, so bilinear to 1 km gives a smooth surface; does not resolve village-scale grazing. Companion: glw4_2020_heads_per_km2_species.tif.

label: Stocking pressure (livestock / grazing capacity)
notes: Sensitivity alternative to livestock_density + grazing_capacity (do not use together with either: double counting). LSU/ha (1 LSU = 1.8 TLU) / grazing capacity LSU/ha; 1 = stocked at capacity. Fixed 0-2 bounds: 2x capacity or more scores 1. Already on the template grid.

label: Share of cell in lower ecological condition (old fields)
notes: Fallow land & old fields (trees, bush, grass, bare, low shrub, wetlands): former cropland with degraded soils and vegetation cover, so lower ecological condition and more sensitive to drought (lower infiltration and water retention, slower recovery, more erosion). Already on the template grid (average of 20 m to 1 km in stage 20), so resample = near. Cells without old fields = 0. trim 0.01: long tail (p99 ~0.66). Spearman with smallholder_presence 0.20. Single date (2022).

label: Share of cell under alien trees (incl. plantations)
source: MapWAPS uMzimvubu (Figshare record 13 Aug 2026; Sentinel-2 15 May 2023), polygons rasterised to 10 m (110/209)
notes: Black wattle, silver wattle, gum, pine, poplar and other aliens; plantations included because pine and gum use the same water planted or invading. More alien trees = less streamflow and baseflow for households drawing from rivers and springs. Already on the template grid (10 m counts summed to 100 m then averaged to 1 km in stage 20), so resample = near. Catchment only: Alfred Nzo cells outside it are NA; cells < 50% mapped are NA. trim 0.01. Wattle is also a fuelwood/pole resource, so keep its weight modest.

label: Share of cell under invasive alien trees (plantations removed)
notes: Sensitivity alternative to alien_tree_cover (do not use both). Pine and gum pixels on SANLC 2022 planted forest (5 dense, 6 open, 7 clear-felled) removed.

label: Share of cell under riparian alien trees
notes: Sensitivity layer. Alien pixels within 100 m of an NFEPA river line (1:500 000 network, so a wider zone than the riparian strip itself) as a share of the mapped cell; 0 where there is no river. Where water use per tree is highest.

label: Share of households involved in agriculture
source: Stats SA Census 2011 H14 Agricultural Households on 2016 wards (SuperWEB2 boundary alignment; 203)
notes: Households with at least one of livestock, poultry, vegetables, other crops, fodder, other (one crossed table, so no double counting) / Census 2011 SAL households summed by 2016 ward. Spread on SANLC settlement to 1 km. na_fill 0: cells without settlement have no households relying on farming (exposure 211 is 0 there), so every cell carries the same set of vulnerability indicators. Full count, 2011. Fixed 0-1 bounds.

label: Households relying on rainfall-dependent water sources (2022)
source: Stats SA Census 2022 by police district (DataFirst casd-2022-policedist v1; 205)
notes: Spring + dam/pool + river/stream + rain-water tank as main source: the sources that fail when rainfall fails (water tankers excluded). Every household in a police district gets the district share; households spread on SANLC 2022 settlement then summed to 1 km, so values change only at district boundaries. Weighted 2022 counts; 40.1% of households in the districts touching the CRA rectangle (unimproved only: 23.7%). Spearman with unimproved_water_2022 0.89 across districts. na_fill 0: cells without households score 0. Fixed 0-1 bounds.

label: Households relying on unimproved water sources (2022, JMP definition)
source: Stats SA Census 2022 by police district (DataFirst casd-2022-policedist v1; 205)
notes: Sensitivity alternative to rainfall_dependent_water_2022 (do not use both). Spring + dam/pool + river/stream (JMP/SDG unimproved; rain-water tanks count as improved). Same method as the primary layer. na_fill 0. Fixed 0-1 bounds.

label: Households relying on unimproved water sources (2011)
notes: Sensitivity alternative (JMP unimproved definition, 2011). Spring + dam/pool + river/stream. SALs < 30 households pooled to sub-place. Households spread on SANLC 2022 settlement then summed to 1 km. na_fill 0. 2011 levels are much higher than 2022 (EC 23.5% vs 10.8%).

label: Share of households with income <= R19,600/yr (Census 2011)
source: Census 2011 annual household income by SAL (DataFirst 517; 210)
notes: No income + R1-19,600 (inchh_1-4) / households; SALs < 30 hh pooled to sub-place/main place/LM. Spread on SANLC 2022 settlement to 1 km. na_fill 0: cells without households score 0. Fixed 0-1 bounds. Spearman with settlement_households 0.04 among populated cells.

label: Relative wealth index
notes: Sensitivity alternative to low_income_share_2011 (do not use both). Higher wealth = lower risk. ~2.4 km tiles, populated tiles only.

label: Rural households per km2 (DWS settlements)
source: DWS WSKS settlement household counts FinYear April 2026 (211)
notes: Households in DWS Rural settlements, placed on SANLC 2022 settlement (classes 47-60) inside each polygon at 100 m and summed to 1 km. Already on the template grid, so resample = near. Cells without a settlement are 0, not NA. log1p before min-max because ~60% of cells are 0 and the tail is long (max ~1,230 households/km2); trim 0.01 puts cells above ~155 households/km2 at 1. Companion with urban settlements: dws_all_households_per_km2_1km.tif. DWS misses ~10% of Census 2022 households (towns, commercial farms).

label: Strategic Water Source Area importance (surface + groundwater)
source: SANBI BGIS surface SWSA: 2021 National + 2017 Sub-national; groundwater SWSA 2017 (Le Maitre et al. 2018; 105/212)
notes: Exposed natural asset: share of regional strategic water supply in the cell; higher = more exposure. 0.5 x surface + 0.5 x groundwater, each = tier-weighted share of the 1 km cell (National 1, Sub-national 0.5; rasterised at 100 m, max where polygons overlap). Surface = 2021 fine-scale National SWSAs plus the 2017 Sub-national surface SWSAs (Pondoland Coast), which the 2021 update did not re-delineate because they were left out of the National set as "water secure"; groundwater = 2017. Already on the template grid, so resample = near. Fixed 0-1 bounds. Condition of the SWSA (aliens, old fields, grazing) is vulnerability; the SWSA x pressure layers in data/processed/nbs/swsa_degradation/ are NbS targeting outputs, not indicators. Sensitivity: w_sw = 2/3 in prepare_swsa().

label: Surface-water SWSA importance (2021 National + 2017 Sub-national)
source: SANBI BGIS 2021 surface SWSA (National) + 2017 Sub-national surface SWSA (105/212)
notes: Component of swsa; do not use with it. Tier-weighted share of cell in surface SWSAs: 2021 National (weight 1), 2017 Sub-national Pondoland Coast (weight 0.5).

label: Groundwater SWSA importance (2017)
notes: Component of swsa; do not use with it. Tier-weighted share of cell in 2017 groundwater SWSAs (Type gw + swgw).
